theme: The question that separates good event briefs from great ones

linkedin.text:
There's one question I wish every CMO and HR VP asked before choosing a corporate event production company.

It's not: "What's your biggest event?"
It's not: "How many destinations do you work in?"
It's not: "Can you send a proposal by Friday?"

The question is this: "Tell me about an event that didn't go to plan — and walk me through the first 15 minutes of your response."

In 16 years of producing corporate conferences, incentive trips, gala dinners and product launches across 130+ destinations, I've sat across from hundreds of decision-makers. The ones who asked that question always ended up with the best events. Not because bad things didn't happen on-site. Because they'd already selected a team built for recovery, not just production.

A team that only knows how to execute a perfect plan is a beautiful liability.

A team that has genuine stories of on-site crises resolved invisibly — that's your actual competitive insurance.

What's the question you always ask that most vendors aren't prepared for? I read every comment.

instagram.text:
Every HR leader asks the same question before hiring an event company: "Can you show me something similar?"

Reasonable. But not the question that actually matters.

The one that matters: "Tell me about an event that went wrong. What happened in the first 10 minutes?"

Anyone can curate a portfolio. What you're really hiring is the team's instinct under pressure.

16 years. 1,500+ events. 130+ destinations. The moments that built our reputation weren't the flawless ones.

facebook.text:
Every HR leader I meet asks the same question before choosing an event production company: "Can you show me something you've done that's similar to what I need?"

It's a reasonable question. But it's not the right question.

The right question is: "Tell me about an event that went wrong and how you fixed it in real time."

Anyone can show you a highlight reel. What matters is what happens when the AV fails at 8:47 AM, the keynote speaker misses the connection, or the venue switches your reserved hall at the last hour.

In 16 years and 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations, the moments that defined our reputation weren't the perfect ones. They were the recoveries.

What question do YOU ask a vendor before signing? Share it below — genuinely curious.
